news.title: Motsepe: Africa must win World Cup
news.lede: SANTA MARIA: CAF President Patrice Motsepe has challenged African football to turn its growing influence on the world stage into tangible results, declaring that the continent must win the FIFA World Cup. He made the statement yesterday during the second day of the CAF Strategy Conference in Santa Maria, Sal Island, Cabo Verde. Motsepe said Africa must focus on investment, stronger football structures and improved standards across all 54 Member Associations to achieve its ambition. “We have to win the World Cup.

PARIS England secured a 3-1 win away to Greece on Friday in the first leg of their 2027 Women’s World Cup play-off. Georgia Stanway gave the Lionesses a first-half lead in Crete before Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo put England firmly in control with two more goals after the break.

news.title: Lionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fight
news.lede: World Cup qualifying playoff: Greece 1-3 England. Stanway, Le Tissier and Russo on target. Sarina Wiegman said she wanted to see a bit more from her side after their fairly underwhelming performance against a hugely unfancied Greek side, despite securing a valuable first-leg victory in their Women’s World Cup playoff tie. Georgia Stanway’s neat finish, Maya Le Tissier’s first England goal and Alessia Russo’s low strike were enough to give England control but a Kallisti Brouksair goal for Greece means that the tie is not definitively over, going into Tuesday’s second leg, and Wiegman acknowledged that England had been “a bit sloppy” at times.

news.title: Ferns coach stresses importance of Panama series in World Cup build-up
news.lede: Football Ferns head coach Michael Mayne says the next two international windows will be critical as his team prepare for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. Mayne wants to identify winning combinations and improve team cohesion, starting with New Zealand’s two-match friendly series against Panama. With limited opportunities to work with his players before the tournament, Mayne says every training session and international fixture will count. “I think 45 contact days with the group, you know, before we ultimately name the (World Cup) squad.

news.title: Northern Ireland 0-4 Portugal: NI World Cup hopes gone from 'improbable to impossible'
news.lede: Highlights: Portugal ease past Northern Ireland at Inver Park. Michael McArdle admits Northern Ireland's chances of beating Portugal in a 2027 Women's World Cup play-off semi-final have "gone from improbable to impossible" after a 4-0 defeat at Inver Park. Underdogs heading into the first-leg tie, the hosts were well beaten and face a mammoth task to overturn the deficit in Tuesday's return in Portimao. McArdle, who took over as Northern Ireland manager in March, felt there were positives in the defeat, but said the scoreline was "sore" and "it hurts".

news.title: Saudi Arabia is shelving one if its big stadium projects. What does it mean for the 2034 World Cup?
news.lede: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup? It was billed as "the most unique stadium in the world," a key pillar of Saudi Arabia's World Cup 2034 plans. But now Neom Stadium, part of the kingdom's ambitious aims to build a 170-kilometer-long (111 miles) city in the desert known as The Line, looks set to be scrapped, with the broader project scaled back significantly.

news.title: Brazilian football great Ronaldinho reportedly set to visit Jamaica in December
news.lede: Brazilian football great Ronaldinho is reportedly set to visit Jamaica in early December, according to reliable sources. The reason for his trip to the island has not been disclosed. Ronaldinho has been participating in a series of exhibition games, playing in four matches in the past three weeks. In June, Ronaldinho signed with Italian Serie C club Ravenna at age 46, more than a decade after retiring.
